summary: Specifies the requirements for an MPLS Transport Profile, a joint effort of ITU and IETF to support the needs of transport networks within the MPLS and PWE3 architectures.

eli5.summary: Phone companies needed MPLS to behave like their older transport networks. This lists what it must do.

questions: what are the requirements for mpls transport profile
how fast must mpls-tp recover from a failure
subtitle: The list of things MPLS must do to work as a carrier-grade packet transport network.

tldr.problem: Carriers wanted packet transport with the reliability and operational simplicity of SDH/SONET and OTN, but not all of MPLS suits transport networks and some transport traits are missing from MPLS.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists 115 numbered requirements for an MPLS Transport Profile (MPLS-TP), covering general behavior, layering, the data and control planes, recovery and QoS. They describe which building blocks the MPLS toolkit must offer.
tldr.outcome: It is a requirements document on the Standards Track, produced jointly by the ITU-T and the IETF, so that the ITU-T can cite it. It specifies no protocol itself.

facts.label: Recovery time
facts.value: 50 ms from fault detection, spans under 1200 km

facts.label: Protection of traffic
facts.value: Up to 100% of traffic on the protected path

today: RFC 5654 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It states requirements only, and the protocol work to meet them is left to other documents.

sections.title: Why a Transport Profile
sections.content:
Demand for bandwidth keeps growing as packet services such as Ethernet, VoIP, VPNs, IPTV and radio access network backhauling spread. For two decades, optical transport (SONET/SDH and the Optical Transport Network, OTN) has given carriers high reliability and operational simplicity. Carriers want packet transport that meets the same benchmarks, with guaranteed service level agreements (SLAs) and the lowest total cost of ownership.

Multi-Protocol Label Switching (MPLS) is already important in transport networks, but not every MPLS capability suits transport operations, and some transport characteristics are not reflected in MPLS. The MPLS Transport Profile (MPLS-TP) combines MPLS packet experience with transport operational practice. This RFC is a joint ITU-T and IETF effort. It is a requirements specification placed on the Standards Track so the ITU-T can cite it as a normative reference.
sections.eli5: Phone companies trust their old lines but want to carry modern data. MPLS is good but not quite right yet, so this lists what to change.

sections.title: Transport Networks and Layers
sections.content:
A transport network carries customer traffic between end points over transport paths that have long holding times, are modified infrequently, and have OAM (operations, administration and maintenance) independent of the client's OAM. In MPLS-TP a transport path corresponds to a label switched path (LSP) or a pseudowire (PW).

The RFC builds on layer networks. A layer network offers a transport service to a client layer and operates independently of whichever client uses it. Smaller monitored domains inside a layer are sublayers. In the transport-service layer, customer traffic is encapsulated, and in the transport-path layer such signals are aggregated and monitored. Paths can be unidirectional, co-routed bidirectional (both directions follow the same route) or associated bidirectional (two paired unidirectional paths that may take different routes).
sections.eli5: Think of stacked delivery trucks: small parcels go in boxes, boxes go on pallets, pallets go on trucks, and each level has its own tracking.

sections.title: General and Layering Requirements
sections.content:
The data plane MUST be a subset of the MPLS data plane, using the minimum applicable subset, and the design SHOULD reuse existing MPLS standards. It MUST interoperate with IETF MPLS (RFC 3031) and PWE3 (RFC 3985) where appropriate, without needing a gateway. MPLS-TP MUST be a connection-oriented packet-switching technology with traffic-engineering capabilities and MUST support point-to-point and point-to-multipoint paths, in unidirectional, co-routed bidirectional and associated bidirectional forms.

The RFC requires that both static management-plane provisioning and dynamic control-plane provisioning be supported, that they can coexist, and that static provisioning does not depend on any control plane. If the management or control plane fails, forwarding, OAM and protection MUST keep working. It MUST be possible to deploy MPLS-TP in rings, including interconnected rings, and rings of at least 16 nodes MUST be supported.

For layering, MPLS-TP MUST be able to carry client layers such as IP, MPLS, Ethernet and ATM, and to run over server layers such as Ethernet, SONET/SDH and OTN, with no operational dependency on either. It MUST be possible to hide MPLS-TP addressing and topology from client layers.
sections.eli5: The new system must be a trimmed-down version of the old one, work with or without a central controller, and carry any kind of cargo on any kind of road.

sections.title: Data Plane and Control Plane
sections.content:
The data plane MUST be operable without any IP forwarding, since it works only on the MPLS label. A transport path on a link MUST be identifiable by a single label, and its source MUST be identifiable at its destination. MPLS-TP MUST support mechanisms to preserve the integrity of customer traffic as the SLA requires and to detect a loss of integrity, and it MUST reliably distinguish client packets from MPLS-TP control packets such as OAM and protection-switching packets.

The control plane is optional, but if it exists it MUST fit within the ITU-T ASON architecture. It MUST be independent of the data plane topology, so that a control-plane failure does not imply a data-plane failure. It MUST be able to set up every connectivity pattern of the data plane, configure OAM and protection, scale gracefully, restart and relearn state without impacting forwarding, and hand control of a path between the management plane and the control plane while minimizing data-plane reconfiguration.
sections.eli5: The part that moves the packets must keep working even if the part that gives it orders goes to sleep.

sections.title: Recovery: Protection and Restoration
sections.content:
MPLS-TP MUST provide protection and restoration. Recovery SHOULD be as similar as possible to what existing transport networks do. It MUST apply at link, transport path, segment, concatenated segment and end-to-end levels, and MUST meet the SLA protection objectives. Two figures stand out: MPLS-TP MUST guarantee 50 ms recovery times from the moment of fault detection in networks with spans under 1200 km, and it MUST be possible to require protection of 100% of the traffic on a protected path.

For protection, MPLS-TP MUST support revertive and non-revertive behavior, 1+1 protection and 1:n protection (including 1:1), and MUST support sharing protection resources among paths that are not needed at the same time. Switching MUST NOT put user data into an uncontrolled loop. Restoration MUST support restoration priority and preemption priority.

Recovery can be triggered by lower-layer fault indications such as loss of light, by OAM, by the management plane, and, where a control plane exists, SHOULD be triggered by it. There MUST be a way to tell administrative actions from other triggers. Operators MUST be able to test protection mechanisms without triggering them, and to see the protection status of all transport paths.
sections.eli5: If a road breaks, traffic must jump to a spare road very fast, and the operators must be able to practice that jump without a real emergency.

sections.title: Rings and Quality of Service
sections.content:
Ring topologies get their own requirements. Recovery mechanisms MUST work in any single ring, including when rings are interconnected, and MUST protect user data crossing several rings. Protection switching in a ring MUST complete within 50 ms from fault detection in a 16-node ring with less than 1200 km of fiber, and that time MUST NOT depend on the number of LSPs crossing the ring. The default ring recovery scheme MUST be bidirectional, revertive switching MUST be supported and be the default, and operators MUST be able to lock out protection on selected spans. The RFC also notes that it identified no requirements that are specific to rings, only ones compatible with the generic recovery requirements.

Quality of service mechanisms are REQUIRED. They must support differentiated services with traffic class separation, SLS provisioning with hard and relative end-to-end bandwidth guarantees, jitter- and delay-sensitive services, fair access within a class, guaranteed resources for in-band control and management traffic, and flexible bandwidth allocation.
sections.eli5: On a circular track, a break must be bypassed very quickly, and important traffic gets reserved lanes.

sections.title: Other Requirements and Security
sections.content:
This RFC does not itself cover network management, OAM, performance monitoring or security. It points to separate documents: an MPLS-TP network management requirements document, an MPLS-TP OAM requirements document that also covers performance monitoring, and the security frameworks for MPLS and GMPLS and for MPLS-TP.

The Security Considerations section is a single line that refers the reader to the security requirements section of the document.
sections.eli5: Some topics, like keeping things safe, have their own separate lists, and this RFC just points to them.

viz.caption: THREE KINDS OF TRANSPORT PATH IN MPLS-TP

items.title: Unidirectional
items.text: Carries traffic in only one direction; point-to-point or point-to-multipoint.

items.title: Co-routed bidirectional
items.text: Forward and backward directions follow the same links and nodes and are managed as one entity.

items.title: Associated bidirectional
items.text: A pair of unidirectional paths associated at the ends; they may take different routes.

viz.caption: PROTECTION SCHEMES REQUIRED BY THE RFC

cells: MUST be supported; SHOULD be the default for 1:n
